description.fun: Cyndaquil is shy enough to curl into a ball when threatened, but the four red spots on its back flare into a crown of flames when it's angry or alarmed, and sputter when it's tired. Its Japanese name, Hinoarashi, mixes fire with porcupine and can be read as 'storm of fire'. It's a first partner twice over: in Johto, and in the Hisui of Legends: Arceus.
description.guide: A small Fire-type Pokémon with four fire-producing spots on its back, one of Johto's first partners and also a first partner in Hisui in Legends: Arceus. It is timid and curls into a ball when threatened, but its flames grow stronger as it gets angry. Its line ends in Typhlosion or, in Hisui, Hisuian Typhlosion.
description.tagline: A timid fire mouse whose back bursts into flame when startled

description.fun: Quilava turns its back on opponents before a battle, on purpose: that's where its flames are, and it fights with them and blasts of superheated air, safe inside its fireproof fur. Its English name was suggested by Jeff Kalles, who helped name Generation 2 and says the companies wanted a Pokémon for every letter of the alphabet. Raised in Hisui, it grows into a ghostly Typhlosion instead.
description.guide: The middle stage of the Cyndaquil line, a slender Fire-type Pokémon with flame vents on its head and rear. It fights with flames and superheated air, protected by non-flammable fur. It evolves into Typhlosion, or into Hisuian Typhlosion in Hisui.
description.tagline: Fights back-first, wreathed in flame and fireproof fur

description.fun: Typhlosion hides behind a shimmering haze of heat, and when it's truly furious anything it touches bursts into flame. Rubbing its fur together sets off explosions, which is why a restless, sleeping Typhlosion is best left alone. Its name blends typhoon with explosion. In Hisui it's a gentle Fire and Ghost type said to guide lost souls home with 108 ghostly flames.
description.guide: The final form of Cyndaquil, a large Fire-type Pokémon that hides in a haze of heat and can cause explosions by rubbing its fur together. Its name blends 'typhoon' and 'explosion'. It has a Fire and Ghost regional form, Hisuian Typhlosion.
description.tagline: A volcanic beast whose rubbing fur sets off explosions

description.fun: Mount Coronet's strange energy made it Fire and Ghost: a calm Typhlosion that gazes into space, said to purify lost spirits with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. Angered, it unleashes 108 ghost flames shaped like ferocious beasts.

note.text: A Quilava that evolves in Hisui, touched by the mysterious energy of Mount Coronet, becomes Hisuian Typhlosion and gains the Ghost type.
